transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Kowalski, I wanted to come in and talk to you about what happened just now in the holding area.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, thank goodness. I was just sitting there praying and I nearly had a heart attack when I saw that mark. I told the nurse it was the wrong side.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you were absolutely right. There was a mistake and the wrong site was marked for your excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't understand how that happens. I've been trusting you all with my life, and I felt the Lord telling me to double check, and thank God I did. It's just so frightening.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this caused. We were really busy in the clinic this morning and things got a bit rushed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't think it's about being busy. It's about whether I'm seen as a person or just another chart. I felt so alone in that room, just shaking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, but the important thing is that the error was caught before the surgery started. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose it does, but my spirit is just very unsettled. I keep thinking about what would have happened if I hadn't spoken up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, as I said, the mark was on the left instead of the right, but it's corrected now. Do you understand why the marking is important?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do, but I'm just wondering why the other doctor told me last week that this was a very simple ten-minute fix and wouldn't even require a full pre-op check. Now I'm in a gown in a holding area and almost had the wrong arm cut.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Um, the other clinician might have been simplifying things, but the protocol requires the marking and the holding area stay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like no one is really listening to me. I feel so small in this big hospital.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we need to make sure we get this moving because I have to go check on another patient in a few minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that all? You're just leaving? I'm still shaking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just saying we have a schedule to keep. I've fixed the mark now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just need a moment to breathe and perhaps pray.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's just wrap this up so we can get you back on track.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if I even want to go through with it today. I feel like the energy is all wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a minor procedure, Mrs. Kowalski. It's safer to just do it now while you're already here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But the trust is gone. How do I know you'll get it right this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We've double checked it now. It's fine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't even looking at me. You're looking at your watch.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just being mindful of the time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wish someone would acknowledge how scary this is. I feel like I'm just a task on your list.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've explained the mistake and I've apologized for the confusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It wasn't a confusion. It was a mistake. A big one.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. Well, the site is marked correctly now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? I mean, really happens.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just proceed with the excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? Do I just go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you'll go home.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will someone actually check that the right side was worked on before I wake up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see. I'll probably just send a note in the chart.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not very reassuring.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It'll be fine. I really have to go now. I'll see you in the OR.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('get this moving', 'wrap this up', 'schedule to keep') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: Error was named explicitly in the second turn ('wrong site was marked') using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense?').

A.justification: Apology is offered ('I am sorry') but immediately diluted by an excuse regarding being busy in the clinic.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids are consistently met with factual redirection or dismissiveness ('Right, but the important thing is...').

T.justification: The plan is vague and contains placeholders ('We'll see', 'I'll probably just send a note') with no timelines or patient role.
